Renovation Column: All I want for Christmas is a new downstairs loo
The paint is dry and the vision is clear but whilst we're so near to finishing a room we're so far from putting the tools away.
After months of cooking on camping stoves and washing pots in a caravan something special happened this week: the much-anticipated arrival of the new kitchen.
True to form it wasn’t all plain sailing with the delivery and who knows how long it will take us to install (it is our first kitchen installation rodeo) but still a milestone moment non the less.
Monday was the day we had been waiting for so we woke up giddy as kids at Christmas and awaited our all important text giving us a two hour delivery time slot.
Hours came and went and as darkness fell hope was dwindling. My husband assured me they could deliver up to 10pm so we kept the dream alive. It wasn’t until my husband re-read the delivery email that stated “week commencing” for delivery rather than "day of" that we admitted defeat.
It would be another two days before our kitchen actually rocked up but when you’ve been without once since June what’s a few more days and a few more microwavable meals in the grand scheme of things.
It had been a manic week in the run up to delivery day as we’d set ourselves the mammoth task of painting the whole space prior to arrival. And as we scraped the 25th litre of paint from the tin at midnight on our third evening of painting you get an idea of the task we had taken on. But we did it, rushing to finish for the fictional Monday delivery day that came and went, but there's nothing like a deadline to light a fire under you.
Now the biggest deadline of all is looming - Christmas -and I feel a little like a stressed out Carol Smiley from Changing Rooms. You know the show where they gave themselves two days to transform a five bed house and then wondered why no one was speaking to each other by the end of it.
Whilst we won't be cooking a Christmas dinner in the new kitchen this year we still would like to spend the festive period in something that resembles a family home rather than a building site.
Christmas presents will also look a little different for us this year – I’m hoping for a new downstairs loo while my husband has a wash basin for the WC at the top of his wish list - who said romance was dead.
The end now feels within reach but the last bit of the process seems to require the most effort. Add to the mix the fact you're in a queue of thousands of other stressed-out families all hoping to get plumbers and electricians back to the house before the big day and it feels a little like the Hunger Games – may the odds be ever in our favour.

Doncaster Wetherspoons' wipe the floor with three separate wins at Loo of the Year Awards
The toilets are judged against numerous criteria, including décor and maintenance and cleanliness
Three Doncaster Wetherspoons have celebrated a win at the Loo of the Year Awards 2026, scooping top honours for their toilet standards.
The Gate House in High Street, Doncaster, and The Old Market Hall in Market Street, Mexborough, have each been awarded a platinum plus grading by inspectors, and The Red Lion in Market Place, Doncaster, has been awarded a platinum grading.

In order to compare, Loo of the Year Awards inspectors made unannounced visits to thousands of toilets at sites across the UK. All of the toilets are graded bronze, silver, gold, platinum, platinum plus or diamond, with unacceptable toilets not graded at all.
The toilets are judged against numerous criteria, including décor and maintenance, cleanliness, accessibility, hand washing and drying equipment, and overall management.
The Gate House manager, Benjamin Leese, said: “We are delighted with the grading. Staff at the pub ensure the toilets are in excellent condition at all times and it is great that this has been recognised by the inspectors.”
The Loo of the Year Awards 2026 managing director, Becky Wall, said: “The toilets at the three pubs have been independently assessed against the Loo of the Year Awards’ 101 criteria, recognising the standard of the facilities, their cleanliness, maintenance and overall presentation. The pubs thoroughly deserve their gradings.”
